patient_visible.chief_complaint: Recurrent cough and sputum for 3 months, worsened with fever for 1 week
patient_visible.present_illness: The patient developed cough 3 months ago without clear precipitating factors, more pronounced in the morning and at night, with yellow-white viscous sputum, moderate volume (~20-30 ml/day), no obvious foul odor. In the past week, cough and sputum have worsened, sputum color changed to yellow-green, volume increased to ~50 ml/day, accompanied by fever (max 38.5°C), more pronounced in the afternoon and evening, with chills, fatigue, and decreased appetite. Self-administered cephalosporin antibiotics for 3 days without significant improvement.
patient_visible.past_history: Hypertension for 5 years, well-controlled on amlodipine 5mg daily (BP 130-140/80-90 mmHg). No history of diabetes, coronary artery disease, hepatitis, or tuberculosis.
patient_visible.personal_history: Smoking: 30 pack-years (1 pack/day for 30 years). Occasional alcohol. Occupation: office worker, no occupational dust/chemical exposure.
patient_visible.family_history: Father diagnosed with lung cancer at age 65. Mother has hypertension. No family history of tuberculosis.
patient_visible.allergies: No known drug or food allergies.

lab_tests.report_text: WBC 12.5×10^9/L (ref 4.0-10.0), Neutrophils 82% (ref 50-70%), Lymphocytes 14%, Hemoglobin 142 g/L, Platelets 280×10^9/L. CRP 68 mg/L (ref <8 mg/L). Impression: Leukocytosis with neutrophilia, markedly elevated CRP — consistent with bacterial infection.
Sputum culture: Streptococcus pneumoniae, colony count >10^5 CFU/ml. Sensitivity: Penicillin-sensitive (MIC 0.03 μg/ml), Ceftriaxone-sensitive, Levofloxacin-sensitive, Erythromycin-resistant.

ALT 35 U/L, AST 30 U/L, Creatinine 78 μmol/L, BUN 5.2 mmol/L, Glucose 5.8 mmol/L. Procalcitonin 2.8 ng/ml (ref <0.05 ng/ml). Impression: Markedly elevated procalcitonin supports bacterial infection diagnosis.

imaging.report_text: Findings: Large patchy high-density consolidation in the posterior segment of the right upper lobe, with ill-defined margins, air bronchogram sign visible within, surrounded by small ground-glass opacity. No enlarged lymph nodes in the right hilum or mediastinum. Left lung field clear. No bilateral pleural effusion.

gold_standard_diagnosis.primary: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (right upper lobe), Streptococcus pneumoniae

key_questions: Presence of chest pain or dyspnea
Smoking history (lung cancer risk factor, combined with family history)
TB exposure history (differential with pulmonary tuberculosis)
key_exams: Chest CT (define lesion nature and extent)
Sputum culture + sensitivity (identify pathogen and guide antibiotics)
key_evidence: Chest CT: RUL consolidation + air bronchogram → classic lobar pneumonia
Procalcitonin 2.8 → strongly suggestive of bacterial infection
Sputum culture: S. pneumoniae → confirmed pathogen
Smoking + lung cancer family history → need to exclude lung cancer (CT shows no mass → preliminarily excluded)

diagnostic_pitfalls: Must differentiate from pulmonary TB: no classic TB symptoms (low-grade fever, night sweats, weight loss) but should ask about TB exposure
Must differentiate from lung cancer: patient has 30 pack-year smoking + family history, but CT shows inflammatory consolidation rather than mass — not consistent with typical lung cancer presentation
Antibiotics ineffective after 3 days: rule out resistant organisms (sensitivity shows erythromycin-resistant but penicillin-sensitive)
